youtube_title: Copshaholm, South Bend: the 38-room Oliver mansion left just as the family had it
body: When the Oliver family gave up their 38-room mansion in South Bend, they left the furniture behind. The Olivers named the house Copshaholm, for the Scottish village James Oliver came from. James Oliver patented his chilled plow in 1857, and his South Bend factory grew into one of the largest plow works in the world. His son, J.D. Oliver, built the mansion of Indiana fieldstone, and the family moved in on New Year's Day, 1897. Olivers lived there for some 75 years. In 1988, the family gave the house to the local historical society, furnishings and all. Today it's part of The History Museum, with guided tours.
